subject: Lighthouse Analytics — service surge snapshot & executive note
messages:
From: Alex Harper <alex.harper@lighthouse-analytics.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: mike.tucker@lighthouse-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Unusual latency and 502s across our tokens — immediate help requested

Hi Marissa,

We saw a major spike in inference latency and a small but growing number of 502 responses starting ~07:50 PST this morning. Our analytics pipelines that call Redwood for batch scoring have ~10% failure and latency is twice the SLA threshold, causing downstream retries and backlog.

Can you confirm whether this is a targeted degradation or related to a regional capacity event? We need a short customer-facing summary with expected restoral time and any mitigation we should take on our side (retry/backoff config, model variant switch).

We’re preparing an internal incident call and I may need an exec-level touchpoint for our COO.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Harper
Head of Platform Engineering
Lighthouse Analytics
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual latency and 502s across our tokens — immediate help requested

Marissa / Olga — FYI and immediate actions taken:
- Confirmed elevated p50/p95 in us-west-2 starting 07:48 PST. Spike correlated with an autoscaler mis-firing for a mixed-traffic pool that hosts several small customers + LHA.
- Applied an emergency horizontal scale and bumped pool size at 08:12 PST; error rate dropped but some in-flight requests still 502.
- Enabled aggressive prefix cache warm-up for the affected model variant, which reduced cold-KV misses.

I’m attaching an initial timeline (sre_timeline_20270222.csv) and a small sample of logs for your review. Next steps: 1) brief customer exec note, 2) schedule postmortem with ops/vendor owners, 3) prepare formal credit calculation if SLA breached.

-Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sre_timeline_20270222.csv; traffic-sample-logs.txt
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Harper <alex.harper@lighthouse-analytics.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Lighthouse Analytics — short status update and immediate mitigations (readout)

Alex — quick update from the on-call and SRE teams. Thanks for flagging this.

What happened (short): A misconfiguration in autoscaler thresholds for a shared inference pool in us-west-2 led to delayed capacity allocation during a sudden queued-load increase. That caused elevated latencies and some 502 responses for requests that timed out or hit transient resource contention.

Impact: Your production scoring traffic experienced ~10% request errors and p95 latency ~2x our SLA during the 07:48–08:20 PST window. We applied emergency scaling and cache warm-up; error rate has fallen to <0.5% and latency is returning to normal.

Immediate mitigations we recommend on your side:
- Keep current retry/backoff settings (exponential, max 3 retries) and consider a temporary increase to max-retries = 4 for non-critical batch jobs through today.
- If feasible, switch to the pinned low-latency model variant we previously validated (variant-id: LLV-2) for high-priority scoring; we can flip routing for you if you want.

What we’re doing next:
- Formal postmortem and timeline (we’ll share a draft in 48 hours).
- Executing a fix to autoscaler thresholds and adding a canary to detect this class of failure.
- Preparing a one-time service credit proposal for the impacted window; will include calculation methodology.

I’ll escalate to my VP and the operations owner; Olga is looping in CS to coordinate the credit/contract path and Ben owns the technical follow-up.

Would you like a short 15-min briefing with our COO and SRE lead this morning at 09:00 PST?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Harper <alex.harper@lighthouse-analytics.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@lighthouse-analytics.com, mike.tucker@lighthouse-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lighthouse Analytics — short status update and immediate mitigations (readout)

Marissa — thanks for the quick update and proposed mitigations. 09:00 PST for a 15-min sync works for our side; please include any runbook excerpts we should keep in-flight.

Two asks up-front (for contracting/legal):
1) We’ll need a short confirmation that no customer data was exfiltrated or persisted beyond normal request handling; this is for our privacy review.
2) Contracts wants the time window for credit calculations and an early estimate so they can prepare the amendment paperwork.

If you can include a brief clause or cover note we can escalate internally to speed processing, that would help.

Thanks — Alex
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Harper <alex.harper@lighthouse-analytics.com>, contracts@lighthouse-analytics.com
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lighthouse Analytics — short status update and immediate mitigations (readout)

Alex / Contracts team — noted and answering both asks below:  

1) Data exposure: Ben’s team completed an initial audit of request/response logs and there is no evidence of data exfiltration or unauthorized persistence. All logs referenced are standard request metadata and stack traces; no application payloads were copied outside our S3 audit store. We will include a signed attestation in the postmortem package.

2) Credit window and estimate: Impact window determined by SRE: 2027-02-22T07:48:00-08:20:00 PST. Based on usage in that window we estimate a preliminary service credit equal to 3% of February usage for your account. We will provide a detailed calculation and a draft amendment for signatures within 48 hours.  

Attachments/links: initial timeline and logs (see attachments) and a working postmortem draft in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/notes/lighthouse-2027-02-22.

We’ve scheduled a 15-minute exec sync at 09:00 PST and will include Ben for ops commentary and Olga for credit/contract coordination. If you prefer a different attendee list, tell me now and we’ll adjust.

Thanks again for the rapid coordination.

—Marissa
Attachment: postmortem-draft-v1.docx
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Postmortem draft & immediate action items (internal)

Team — great work on the rapid restoral. Collating the notes from today:
- Root cause: autoscaler threshold regression during traffic spike (INF-9843).
- Immediate actions completed: emergency scale, cache warm-up, temporary routing to LLV-2 for high-priority jobs.
- Next actions (owners & ETA):
  * Ben: finalize SRE timeline and log snippets; deliver by 2027-02-23 09:00 PST (attachment: sre_timeline_20270222.csv).
  * Olga: prepare credit calculations and draft amendment for Contracts; deliver by 2027-02-24 EOD.
  * David: review proposed long-term mitigations (canary autoscaler change + monitoring) and commit code review owners; deliver by 2027-02-25.
  * Marissa: finalize customer-facing postmortem & attestation; share with Alex and Contracts within 48 hours (attachment: postmortem-draft-v1.docx).

I’ve linked the Jira for the work and left a first-pass postmortem in Drive. Please update the draft directly — we need a concise customer-facing one-pager and an internal technical appendix.

Thanks — Marissa
